title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2020 Measures No. 5) Bill 2020
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2020 Measures No. 5) Bill 2020

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change tax treatment of eligible pandemic business grants, enable direct transfers of unclaimed superannuation to KiwiSaver and recognise a deductible gift recipient.
Grant relief would require an eligible state or territory program declared by the minister and a business with aggregated turnover below $50 million.
Neighbourhood Watch Australasia would receive deductible gift recipient status for gifts from 1 July 2019, while KiwiSaver transfers would be subject to commencement arrangements.
changes: Covered grant payments would be classified as non-assessable non-exempt income.
Individuals could direct the Taxation Commissioner to pay held superannuation amounts to a KiwiSaver provider.
Interest could be payable on amounts transferred to KiwiSaver.
summary.affected: Eligible businesses, people with unclaimed superannuation moving money to New Zealand, Neighbourhood Watch Australasia and its donors are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The bill makes eligible state and territory coronavirus business grants tax-free, including Victorian grants announced 13 September 2020, allows direct transfer of unclaimed super from New Zealand residents to KiwiSaver funds, and adds Neighbourhood Watch Australasia Limited to the list of deductible gift recipients.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Jones
speeches.brief: The speaker moved a second reading amendment to the Treasury Laws Amendment Bill, arguing the government's pandemic economic support has been insufficient and that state and territory governments—including those led by Dan Andrews, Mark McGowan, Annastacia Palaszczuk, Andrew Barr, and Michael Gunner—have borne the costs. The amendment also calls on the government to commit to legislated superannuation increases, noting the Prime Minister receives 15.4% superannuation while proposing 9.5% for others.
